course_name_original: Aprovechamiento Energético de Recursos Hidráulicos y Eólicos
course_name_en: Energy Exploitation of Hydraulic and Wind Resources
prerequisites: Competences and learning outcomes from Bachelor's degree subjects, especially those related to fluid mechanics, electricity, mechanisms, construction, and business management.
Linguistic competence in Spanish and English (reading level).
Calculator skills and ability to create and manage graphs.

learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context.

Students should know how to apply acquired knowledge and their problem-solving ability in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study.

Students should be able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of forming judgments based on information that, being incomplete or limited, includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Students should know how to communicate their conclusions and the ultimate knowledge and reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Students should possess learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous manner.

Have adequate knowledge of the scientific and technological aspects of: mathematical, analytical and numerical methods in engineering, electrical engineering, energy engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, continuum mechanics, industrial electronics, automation, manufacturing, materials, quantitative management methods, industrial informatics, urban planning and infrastructure.
Design, calculate and engineer products, processes, facilities and plants.
Conduct research, development and innovation in products, processes and methods.
Carry out strategic planning and apply it to construction and production systems, quality and environmental management.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Engineer.
Knowledge and ability for the analysis and design of electrical energy generation, transmission and distribution systems.
Knowledge and abilities for the design and analysis of thermal machines and engines, hydraulic machines and industrial heating and cooling installations.
Knowledge and abilities that allow understanding, analyzing, exploiting and managing the different energy sources.
Knowledge about construction, building, installations, infrastructures and urban planning in the field of industrial engineering.
Knowledge and abilities for the calculation and design of structures.

Knowledge and abilities to project and design electrical and fluid installations, lighting, air conditioning and ventilation, energy saving and efficiency, acoustics, communications, home automation and smart buildings and security installations.
Knowledge and abilities to perform verification and control of installations, processes and products.
Knowledge and abilities to carry out certifications, audits, verifications, tests and reports.
Apply rationally the principles of hydraulic and wind renewable energy conversion.
Evaluate the available hydraulic and wind resources in a given area or environment.
Work on practical cases of general design, basic equipment sizing, modeling, analysis and regulation of hydraulic and wind power plants.
Understand and apply the operation and management strategies of hydraulic and wind resource conversion plants.

syllabus_topics: Types of hydraulic exploitations, equipment, and operation strategies.
Infrastructure and equipment of hydraulic power plants.
Types, performance, and operation of hydraulic turbines.
Types, performance, and operation of wind turbines.
Planning and management of wind farms.

assessment_methods.method: Activities in laboratory practices and visits to power plants
Activities in classroom practices (practical and numerical exercises)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary assessment, the final grade is 40% from the final exam and 60% from practical activities (30% from lab practices and visits, 30% from classroom practices). To pass, a non-zero score must be obtained in each block of the exam, and a minimum of 4 out of 10 points on the exam itself is required. For extraordinary assessments and differentiated evaluation, the exam accounts for 80% and practical activities for 20%. Scores from practical classes are valid for the ordinary call of the current academic year. Clarity, grammar, mathematical expression, knowledge, theoretical approach, terminology, reasoning, and precision of numerical results are valued in all assessments.
